title: Coral Cell Dissociation and Sampling Protocol
author: Liza M M Roger
materials: Coral Rx coral dip disinfectant solution

Mix the following reagents in 1 L of deionized water. 23 g Sodium chloride (NaCl) 0.763 g of Potassium chloride (KCl) 3 g of Sodium sulfate (NaSO4) 0.25 g of Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). Autoclave and sterile filter (0.22 µm)

steps.title: Cut coral fragment and transfer
steps.instruction: Using sterile clippers, cut a single coral fragment (nubbin) approximately 1 cm in length and place it into a crystallizing dish containing artificial seawater (ASW).

steps.title: Rinse fragment with filtered seawater
steps.instruction: Rinse the nubbin with filtered artificial seawater (FASW) using a 1 mL pipette tip, performing 5–10 gentle passes on each side, aspirate the wash, add 4 mL fresh FASW to the dish, and repeat the rinse two more times for a total of three rinses.

substeps.instruction: Perform 5–10 passes of FASW on each side of the nubbin with a 1 mL tip.
Add 4 mL fresh FASW to the dish.
Repeat the rinse procedure twice more (total three rinses).

steps.title: Detach cells with CMF‑ASW wash
steps.instruction: After incubation, gently pipette CMF–ASW onto the nubbin to detach surface cells; the nubbin will turn pale‑white and the suspension will become turbid.

steps.title: Centrifuge cell suspension (first spin)
steps.instruction: Transfer the cell suspension (without the nubbin) to a fresh sterile conical tube and centrifuge at 1200 rpm (204 RCF) for 3 min at 25 °C.

steps.title: Prepare coral cell culture medium
steps.instruction: In the biosafety cabinet, prepare 50 mL of culture medium in a sterile conical tube by adding 7.5 mL DMEM (15 % final), 5 mL FBS (10 % final), 250 µL anti‑anti (0.5 % final), 250 µL gentamicin (0.5 % final), then bring the volume to 50 mL with 37 mL FASW and gently mix.

substeps.instruction: Add 37 mL FASW to reach 50 mL total.

steps.title: Resuspend cells in culture medium
steps.instruction: After the first centrifugation, discard the supernatant, add 1 mL of the prepared coral cell culture medium, and gently resuspend the cell pellet.

steps.title: Collect and store time‑zero samples
steps.instruction: Immediately after dissociation, aliquot the cell suspension into two microcentrifuge tubes (MCT) for T0 sampling—one for 25 °C and one for 30 °C—centrifuge each at 8000 rpm (6010 RCF) for 10 min at 4 °C, then store the pellets at –20 °C until protein extraction; repeat sampling at 6, 12, 18, and 24 h as needed.

substeps.instruction: Place 1 mL of suspension into a tube for 25 °C and another for 30 °C.
Centrifuge at 8000 rpm (6010 RCF) for 10 min at 4 °C.
Collect additional samples at 6 h, 12 h, 18 h, and 24 h.

steps.title: Disinfect fragment in Coral Rx solution
steps.instruction: Add approximately 2.64 mL of Coral Rx coral dip disinfectant to 500 mL of ASW in a crystallizing dish and incubate the fragment in this solution for 10 min with constant aeration.

steps.title: Return fragment and image nubbin
steps.instruction: After the 10‑minute disinfection, return the coral fragment to the aquarium tank, transfer the nubbin to a sterile glass petri dish, and capture an image with a scale.

steps.title: Transfer nubbin to petri dish with FASW
steps.instruction: In the biosafety cabinet, use sterile tweezers to move the nubbin into a sterile plastic petri dish and add 4 mL of filtered sterile artificial seawater (FASW, 0.22 µm) using a 5 mL serological pipette.

steps.title: Incubate nubbin in CMF‑ASW
steps.instruction: Prepare a 15 mL sterile conical tube containing 3 mL calcium‑magnesium‑free artificial seawater (CMF‑ASW, 0.22 µm), transfer the rinsed nubbin into this tube, and incubate for 1 hour in the biosafety cabinet under ambient light.

steps.title: Stain cells with SYTOX and Hoechst
steps.instruction: To 1 mL of cell suspension, add 10 µL SYTOX Orange (final 0.2 µM) and 2 µL Hoechst 33342 (final 40 µM).

steps.title: Incubate stains in dark
steps.instruction: Incubate the stained suspension in the dark for 30 min while starting the plate reader.

steps.title: Post‑stain centrifugation and medium replacement
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the stained cells for 3 min at 1200 rpm (204 RCF) at 25 °C, discard the staining solution, and resuspend the pellet in coral culture medium.

steps.title: Hemocytometer counting and imaging
steps.instruction: Place 10 µL of the stained cell suspension into a hemocytometer chamber, image using Brightfield, DAPI, TRITC, GFP, and CY5 channels at 4× and 20× magnification, and calculate cell concentration with C = c / (d × A × f) where c = average cells counted, d = chamber depth (0.1 mm Neubauer or 0.2 mm F‑Rosenthal), A = counted area (mm²), f = 1000 mm³/mL. Use channel definitions: DAPI = total cells, TRITC = dead cells, CY5 = symbiont algae, GFP = host cells; compute viability = ([DAPI] – [TRITC]) / [DAPI] × 100.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL stained cells to hemocytometer.
Capture images in BF, DAPI, TRITC, GFP, CY5 at 4× and 20×.
Count cells and apply the concentration formula.
Interpret channels: DAPI = total cells, TRITC = dead cells, CY5 = symbiont algae, GFP = host cells.

steps.title: Plate cells for temperature time‑points
steps.instruction: Obtain two 24‑well plates; add 1 mL of cell suspension (~1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹) to each well designated for a time‑point, add extra medium around the plate edges to prevent evaporation, and incubate one plate at 25 °C and the other at 30 °C.
